observations: Chromium groups pass 39 checks and 15 complete native member images. Normal/disabled/focus, native disabled skipping and stopping boundaries, Shift selection/focus separation and Space actions use actual seat input.

Original trusted click/input/change behavior and original click cancellation/rollback pass. Removing, regrouping or changing a focused target type cancels stale radio activation; removing the original key target cancels its gesture.

Original backend node IDs independently verify group metadata for separate forms, unnamed controls, unowned controls, shadow scopes and an external form-associated member. Hidden checked data does not add a fake native cell.

Detach/reinsert retains the original DOM ID, recreates the native group with a fresh control ID and passes a subsequent trusted action and native image comparison. Helper logs show exactly 6 live matrices for 6 groups and no individual kind 3 radio controls.

The prior first pointer test sent fractional compositor coordinates; the command was rejected. Tests now round measured coordinates and assert command success. A later image mismatch was the real desktop cursor overlay; the cursor is moved outside complete member captures.

Final helper/reference stderr includes external system-clock correction notices, retained in runtime metadata. Owned compositor and browser exit0; helper/capture are intentionally stopped with SIGTERM. No candidate adapter remains mapped.
open: Complete pointer semantics, disabled-cell native actions, outside-release actions and label activation; current browser proof covers ordinary enabled pointer activation only.

Native layout topology beyond the current one-column model, CSS visibility variants, large groups and efficient member rendering. The common host currently renders a complete matrix per requested member.
Actual browser zoom/mixed/fractional/HiDPI mapping and group recovery through the session supervisor. The shared cache stores epochs, but browser recovery is not claimed from that data alone.

Gecko group binding using the same common cache/provider, remaining browser controls/shortcuts/menus and accessibility/IME requirements, derivatives, installed deployment, followed by GTK/Qt/KDE integration.
